thread:
maria: Heads-up — I ran a profiler on the canary after yesterday's queue_policy tweak. Seeing regressions for mid-length prompts (~200-600 tokens) when decode rate is high (>60 tok/s). p95 latency up ~18% on the A100 pool. Posting snippets and configs below. Can we discuss tuning the continuous-batching heuristics (bucketing + token budgets)?

sam: Can you paste the classifier thresholds and the token_budget config you used?

maria: Sure — here's the runtime config used in the canary:
```
classifier:
  prompt_len_buckets: [64, 256, 1024]   # boundaries: <=64, 65-256, 257-1024
  decode_rate_buckets: [40, 80]          # boundaries: <40, 40-80, >80 tok/s
runtime:
  token_budget_target_per_batch: 1200
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  queue_policy: "age_weighted"
```
Also saw KV cache miss rate jump from 2.1% -> 5.7% for the mid prompts. Suspect prefix trimming + batching reordering is evicting useful cache entries.

anjali: If decode_rate bucket >80, we should lower token_budget_target to avoid large batches that stall fast decodes. Suggest mapping: >80 -> 900, 40-80 -> 1200, <40 -> 1500.

liam: Agreed on lowering budget for high decode rates. Also noticed kernel selection oddity: for seq=512 padded_to=528 the selector picks a slower fp16 matmul kernel (auto-pad rounding issue). We should add a seq-length alignment heuristic so we prefer kernels optimized for the actual logical length rather than padded size alone.

sam: Can you share the repro command for that kernel fallback?

liam:
```
./profiles/run --model opt-1.3b --seq 512 --pad_align 16 --print-kernel
# shows chosen kernel: matmul_fallback_fp16_sm80 (slower path)
```
If we detect pad-induced kernel switches, we can try small adjustments before batching to avoid that alignment.

perf-bot: Regression alert -> queue_policy v2 (deployed 2026-03-15 14:02 UTC): p50 +4%, p95 +18% on eng-runtime A100 pool. Error rate unchanged. Correlated signals: higher batching latency in bucket prompt_len 256-600 AND decode_rate >60 tok/s.

maria: TL;DR proposed immediate remediation:
1) revert queue_policy tweak for the mid prompt-length bucket (use previous size_priority for that bucket only)
2) implement token_budget_target per decode_rate bucket (anjali to own)
3) preserve first N tokens in KV cache during prefix trimming (experiment with N=128) to reduce miss churn
4) add verbose kernel selection logging so we can detect pad-alignment induced fallbacks in the wild

anjali: I'll take (2) and (3). Plan small perf matrix tomorrow: token_budget targets [800, 1000, 1400] cross product preserve_kv_prefix [64, 128, 256]. I'll post a short table in this thread.

sam: I'll add kernel-selection logging to the runtime behind a debug flag and a lightweight metric (kernel_mismatch_count). Quick patch: if padded_to % 32 != 0 then check alternate selector path.

liam: I'll run the canary with the adjusted token budgets + preserve_kv_prefix=128 behind feature flag `fb/heuristic-decode-buckets`. Will also include a repro where we force pad_align=16 to validate kernel changes.

maria: Great. Please gate changes behind the feature flag and don't flip globally until we have canary numbers. Post raw p50/p95/p99 + KV miss rate per bucket. :thumbsup:

sam: One small note — we should add a per-bucket safety cap for max_batch_tokens (e.g., mid-bucket cap = 2048) to avoid pathological batches when many low-decode-rate requests sneak into the same batch.

maria: Agreed. Add that to the experiment matrix.

anjali: Will do. I'll start the runs first thing and update by EOD PST.

liam: I'll schedule a short sync after results (15m).

maria: Thanks all — high priority for perf stability. If anyone sees a quick rollback path for the queue_policy flag in prod, post it here. :eyes:
